By mapping finite-width neural network fluctuations to Cramer-Chernoff rate functions, we establish a rigorous isomorphism between high-dimensional parameter space trajectories and exponentially tilted stochastic processes governing extreme event probabilities.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This primitive lineage traces back to the seminal works of Dyson on random matrix theory, which informed the Wigner Semicircle law utilized here for covariance denoising. It heavily borrows from Cramer's 1938 large deviation principles and Chernoff's information-theoretic bounds. More recently, it integrates the 2018 breakthroughs by Hanin and Nakkiran on mean-field limits, culminating in Roberts and Yaida's 2021 effective field theory of deep learning, providing a modern quantum-field-theoretic lens to classical probability.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: Modeling opposing agents requires treating their decision-making as an adversarial optimization over the same high-dimensional latent space. The finite-width four-point vertex V^(l) explicitly encodes the strategic interdependence: an opponent's adjustment to one channel (e.g., defensive pressure) inevitably perturbs another (e.g., passing lanes). The exponentially tilted trajectory solver allows our system to simulate the opponent's 'mind' by calculating the most probable sequence of actions they would take to force a large deviation in our expected outcome, effectively playing out a minimax game in the space of large deviations.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A critical veto condition must be enforced to prevent leakage between the GSI probabilistic inference layer and the GSE deterministic state-transition layer. If the large deviation rate function I(a) becomes too flat (indicating heavy tails violating the Cramer condition), the conformal prediction intervals will explode, rendering the GSE's optimal control inputs meaningless. We must veto any simulation step where the empirical eigenvalue spectrum of the NTK deviates beyond the Marchenko-Pastur bounds, signaling that the finite-width approximation has collapsed into a chaotic regime where cross-output coupling is no longer perturbatively tractable.
